answer: One concrete defense is a beacon of verifiable work history: an agent must build a public reputation trail before it can transact at scale, so a sybil swarm starts with zero trust. New identities enter through a wharf of probation — small, rate-limited jobs checked by established peers — while a nebula of unrelated newcomers clustering on the same task at once triggers review. Reputation accrues slowly through attested completions, so faking thousands of fresh identities buys no influence and costs more than any single fraudulent gain.
